payload.title: git_object_id is not the one owner of the git object hash and format: main_anchor._object_oid computes the same object id as blob_object_id and picks the digest by 'oid_length == 64', git's format spelling is mapped in git_containment, state_store (a raw KeyError on an unknown spelling) and the lift, and nothing detects it, because test_git_object_id.py does not test blob_object_id
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/main_anchor.py:334-338 (_object_oid: the object header, sha1 or sha256 by 'oid_length == 64')
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/main_anchor.py:381 (the call in _read_verified, which re-hashes each object against its id)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/git_object_id.py:90-92 (blob_object_id: the same hash for a blob)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/git_object_id.py:39-43 (ObjectFormat, the owner, valued by id length; no parse of git's spelling)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/git_containment.py:265 (_OBJECT_FORMATS: a string-to-string table of git's two spellings)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/git_containment.py:943 (the lookup of the rev-parse --show-object-format answer, refusing object_format_unresolvable)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/state_store.py:2245 (ObjectFormat[...strip().upper()], new in the D6-SEC diff: an unknown spelling raises a raw KeyError)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/validation.py:631 (ObjectFormat(len(oid)): the format taken from the id's length)
aria-kernel/tests/test_git_object_id.py:15-21 (the imports: blob_object_id is not among them)
aria-kernel/tests/test_git_object_id.py:33-43 (the restatement scan: id regexes and len(...) == 40 tests only)
payload.rule_violated: One owner per concept: git_object_id.py names itself the one owner of what a git object id is (ARIA-LOW-518) and owns ObjectFormat, and the D6-SEC fix commit says blob_object_id is now the one owner of the blob hash; every other module reads a hash and a format through it
payload.notes: Registered by the D6-SEC findings clerk from the D6-SEC review round 1 (lens ssot), re-checked at head d460f7917 before registration; non-blocking at merge. Close condition: Two parts, both required. (1) The hash: git_object_id has one object_id(kind, body, ObjectFormat) (blob_object_id is its blob case), main_anchor._object_oid is deleted and _read_verified reads through it; test_git_object_id checks blob_object_id and the new function against git hash-object for sha1 and sha256, and its restatement scan fails on a hashlib.sha1 or sha256 construction over an object header outside the owner. (2) The format: git_object_id gains one parse of the rev-parse --show-object-format answer (and the id-length mapping, if the lift keeps it) that refuses an unknown spelling by a named error; git_containment, state_store, validation and main_anchor read a format through it; tests: an unknown spelling raises the named error, not KeyError, and the scan also fails on a second spelling table or length-to-format test.
